editorial:
If you love a good revenge story with a tough guy at the center, this one is right up your alley. Jason Statham plays a quiet, mysterious new hire at a Los Angeles cash truck company, and from the very first scene you can tell something is off about him. He barely talks, keeps to himself, and seems almost bored by everything around him. But when a heist goes down and his co-workers are in danger, he suddenly shows off scary-good shooting skills that leave everyone stunned. The crew starts asking questions, and you will too. The movie slowly peels back layers of his past, revealing that his real reason for being there is deeply personal and tied to a tragedy that happened months earlier.

The action scenes are sharp and well-shot, with a gritty feel that keeps you on edge. Statham is perfectly cast here, doing what he does best with very few words. The supporting cast is solid, and the story moves at a steady pace that never drags. On the downside, some of the dialogue feels a bit stiff, and a few plot twists are easy to guess if you pay close attention. Still, the final act delivers a satisfying payoff. If you enjoy crime thrillers with a dark edge, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: It turns out Statham's character is actually a crime boss whose son was killed during a cash truck robbery. He took the security guard job to find the crew responsible. In the final scenes, he tracks them down and confronts them during another heist at the depot. A massive shootout breaks out, and he kills the men who murdered his son. The movie ends with him walking away, having completed his revenge, though he is clearly a changed and broken man.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves revenge stories, Jason Statham movies, or gritty crime thrillers.
